quiz.q: Why should you pilot a training before running a ToT on it?
options: To find and fix problems while they are cheap, before they spread through the cascade
To avoid writing a trainer guide
quiz.explain: Piloting reveals weak points in design and materials before many trainers copy them.

quiz.q: A friend reading your trainer guide keeps asking 'what do I do here?'. What does this tell you?
options: She is not a good trainer
The guide has gaps that need clearer instructions
The guide is too short to print
You should remove the guide from the package
quiz.explain: Every hesitation shows a gap. A good guide lets someone deliver without the author present.

quiz.q: A training costs 120,000 naira in total for 20 participants before contingency. With a 10 percent contingency, what is the cost per participant?
On a power and interest grid, where does a funder who controls the budget and wants regular results belong?
quiz.explain: High power and high interest stakeholders should be managed closely with regular contact and clear reports.

quiz.q: Which result statement is clearest and most honest for a partner?
options: The training was a huge success and changed lives
17 of 20 could complete a sales record after training, up from 2; at six weeks, 12 of 18 reached said they record daily
Business profits doubled because of our training
quiz.explain: It states change, numbers and evidence without overclaiming.

quiz.q: In a 90-day plan, when do new trainers usually need the most support?
options: In their first few sessions after the ToT
Never, if the ToT was good
quiz.explain: New trainers drift most from the guide early, so close support in the first sessions protects quality.

finalQuiz.q: Hauwa trains 10 trainers, each of whom runs 2 sessions of 25 women. If 2 trainers drop out completely, what is the reach?
Which Knowles assumption is a trainer using when she asks participants to share their own experience of credit before teaching about loans?
options: Adults' experience is a resource for learning
Adults need tests to stay motivated
finalQuiz.explain: Knowles described adults' experience as a rich resource; drawing it out first connects new content to what they know.

finalQuiz.q: A session starts with a short case story, then pair discussion, then a 10-minute input, then participants plan how they will use the idea. This follows:
finalQuiz.explain: Experience, reflection, concept and application are Kolb's four stages.

finalQuiz.q: Before a session you notice the venue has steps and a participant uses a wheelchair. What should you do first?
options: Proceed and help carry her in
Find a ground floor or accessible venue, or arrange a safe accessible entry, before the day
Move the training online without telling anyone
finalQuiz.explain: Inclusion means planning access in advance so she can participate with dignity.

finalQuiz.q: Which is the correct order of ADDIE?
finalQuiz.explain: ADDIE stands for Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, Evaluation.

finalQuiz.q: Which objective is written at the Apply level of Bloom's taxonomy?
options: List the three types of savings
Calculate the repayment on a 30,000 naira loan using the group's rate
finalQuiz.explain: Calculating with a method in a new case is Apply. 'Appreciate' is not observable.

finalQuiz.q: A two-hour session plan has 150 minutes of activities. What is the best fix?
options: Cut activities that do not serve an objective and shorten input, keeping practice time
Remove the practice to save time
finalQuiz.explain: Activities must serve objectives; practice is where most learning happens, so protect it.

finalQuiz.q: In a microteaching cycle, what happens after a trainee receives feedback?
options: She re-plans and re-teaches the segment
Nothing, feedback is the final step
finalQuiz.explain: The cycle is plan, teach, feedback, re-plan, re-teach.

finalQuiz.q: An observer scores a new trainer's session and finds she changed a key safety step. In a well-designed trainer guide, safety steps should be:
options: Core content that must not change
finalQuiz.explain: Safety rules, facts, key steps and tests are core content and must be delivered as designed.

finalQuiz.q: A participant asks you to lend her money privately during the training. What is the most ethical response?
options: Lend it quietly so nobody knows
Kindly decline, explain you cannot mix personal loans with your trainer role, and point her to appropriate options if available
Announce the request to the group
Give her money from the training budget
finalQuiz.explain: Trainers must keep money transparent and avoid conflicts of interest arising from their position of trust.

finalQuiz.q: Pre-test average 3.0 out of 10, post-test average 7.5 out of 10. What does this show?
options: Participants' learning (Kirkpatrick Level 2) improved by 4.5 points
finalQuiz.explain: Pre and post tests measure learning, Level 2. They do not prove behaviour or results.

finalQuiz.q: Ladi's training costs 90,000 naira for 15 participants, plus a 10 percent contingency. What is the cost per participant?

capstone.title: ToT portfolio: a tested training package and cascade plan
capstone.brief: Design, pilot and evaluate a short training (two to three hours) for a real group in your community, then package it so other trainers can deliver it. Submit a portfolio with needs analysis, SMART objectives, session plan, trainer guide, evaluation results, a reflection on what changed after feedback, and a 90-day cascade plan.
steps: Carry out a needs analysis with at least five future participants and confirm training is the right solution.
Write three to five SMART objectives with Bloom's levels and a timed session plan using Kolb's cycle.
Prepare the package: trainer guide (core and flexible content marked), participant materials, consent and attendance forms, reaction form and pre and post test.
Deliver the session to a real group of at least eight people, with an observer using the checklist.
Calculate reaction and pre and post test averages and write a one-page evaluation report.
Revise the package based on the feedback and data, and write a short reflection on what changed.
Write a costed proposal and a 90-day plan to train other trainers and follow up on quality.
evidence: Needs analysis notes and SMART objectives with Bloom's levels
Session plan with planned and actual timings
Trainer guide and participant materials (version 1 and revised version)
Attendance totals and consent forms (stored securely, not shared publicly)
Reaction results and pre and post test averages
One-page evaluation report including limits of the data
Reflection on what changed after feedback
Costed proposal and dated 90-day cascade plan
